title: Offcut — native WebMCP cutting plans, shared state, separate approval
description:
Offcut is a shared cutting-stock workbench for workshops and makerspaces. People enter usable stock and exact parts, protect stock records, inspect real layouts and release one exact reviewed cut sheet. Why WebMCP? A browser agent discovers six native tools and works on that same committed job, with explicit plan identities, revisions and review state—not a separate website chatbot.

Live workbench: https://ilyanaxo.github.io/offcut-webmcp/
Public MIT source: https://github.com/ilyanaxo/offcut-webmcp
Use, run and test guide: https://ilyanaxo.github.io/offcut-webmcp/guide.html

A real model chooses native Chrome WebMCP calls through an external browser-client harness. The right-hand receipt panel belongs to that separate recording harness, not a chatbot inside Offcut. This is not a ChatGPT screen recording. UI navigation, measurement edits, acknowledgement, approval and download controls are automated for the recording. There is no registered approval tool; this capability boundary is not cryptographic proof of human presence. Waiting time is trimmed, not an end-to-end latency benchmark.

Illustrative sample, not customer or physically verified workshop measurements: 14 parts totalling 7,000 mm; A-01 stays protected. One homogeneous material/cross-section batch uses usable lengths after trim and defect allowances. With one 3 mm kerf per part, including the last, and a 400 mm reusable-remnant threshold, the optimal least-stock/fewer-board sample opens 7,200 mm on 3 boards: 42 mm sawdust + 158 mm short scrap = 200 mm waste, with 0 mm reusable. Keeping useful offcuts opens 10,080 mm on 6 boards: 42 mm sawdust, 0 mm short scrap and 3,038 mm reusable. Reusable remnants and unopened stock are not waste. This uses 2,880 mm more opened stock and handles 3 more boards to avoid 158 mm of short scrap—not measured money, time or carbon savings, physical cutting or actual remnant reuse.

Review stays unapproved until the separate acknowledgement and Approve cut sheet actions in the UI. The actual CSV carries the full approved plan ID in its filename and content; its 17 columns include Part ID so identical part labels remain distinguishable. A different selected draft cannot inherit approval.

Typing kerf 4 while saved kerf is 3 preserves the saved revision: pending edits block staging without blurring or saving. Saving creates revision 2, invalidates approval and makes the old plan stale. The agent replans all 14 parts with 56 mm of sawdust. The ending is REVISION 2 — STAGED, NOT APPROVED; the acknowledgement remains unchecked. Offcut itself needs no application account, model key or backend; the external model client is separate.

Demo sequence
Shared workbench and protected stock
Illustrative measurements and people-owned controls
External model and real native browser tools
Three complete objectives and honest search status
Real layouts: stock, short scrap and useful remnants
Review first; separate UI acknowledgement and approval
Exact approved CSV; drafts cannot inherit approval
Pending edit, committed revision and stale-plan recovery
Revision 2: staged, not approved; public workbench and limits

Original English script and captions; narration synthesized locally with Piper, en_US-ljspeech-high. Voice model: Bryce Beattie; LJ Speech dataset: Keith Ito and Linda Johnson. Creator/dataset public-domain declarations: https://brycebeattie.com/files/tts/ and https://keithito.com/LJ-Speech-Dataset/ . The jurisdiction scope is recorded in submission/media-rights.json: USA public-domain declarations are not unconditional worldwide clearance; the entrant must confirm applicable rights. No human narrator endorsement is claimed. Original Offcut app visuals; no third-party music, stock footage or copied workshop photographs. Captions use Liberation Sans under SIL OFL 1.1; the font license does not apply to output documents, and font files are not redistributed.

These are planning estimates, not machine instructions or a safe-cutting guarantee. Verify actual usable lengths, stock identity, kerf and safe workholding at the bench.
